She said the investigation requested data from the relevant companies covering the period when Mikautadze allegedly handed the money to Liluashvili. Berdzenishvili said an analysis of mobile phone data and internet traffic showed that the two men were in the same place at the same time.

“The prosecution also requested documents relating to the alleged handover of the bribe,” she added.

The prosecutor said the case contains direct evidence supported by other materials, and that there are no objective grounds to question its credibility.

Berdzenishvili said the defence argument that no third parties were present when the money changed hands was not significant to the case. According to her, demands for and payments of bribes generally do not take place in public or in the presence of large numbers of people.

Asked whether Mikautadze went directly to the SSS and handed the money to Liluashvili, Berdzenishvili replied: “Yes. According to the witness, that is what happened.”

The prosecutor said the investigation had also questioned other people who had previously visited Liluashvili. According to their testimony, the procedure for receiving visitors was not always the same.

“The witness also described how he entered the relevant office after undergoing a security check and other procedures. Other people who had previously visited Grigol Liluashvili were also questioned about how they entered the building. Security staff recorded the entry procedure and noted that it did not always involve issuing a pass, a search and so on. In other words, the defendant himself decided how visitors would enter his office,” Berdzenishvili said.

According to her, these circumstances and other factual evidence in the case support the reliability of the information Mikautadze provided to the court.

Berdzenishvili said Mikautadze told the businessmen that the money was being handed over in the interests of the state. According to the prosecutor, one of the businessmen also confirmed this.

“According to the witness, he told the businessmen that this was being done in the interests of the state. One of the businessmen also confirmed this during questioning. They presented the payment as something that served the state’s interests, although this was merely a formal justification. Of course, it was clear to everyone involved that it did not actually serve any state interest,” the prosecutor said.

Berdzenishvili also confirmed that, according to the investigation, Mikautadze brought the money to Liluashvili’s office in a bag.

“Yes, he had the money in his bag. As for his presence in the building, we questioned a security guard who confirmed that he saw Romeo Mikautadze, for example, on the same floor,” she said.

Journalists also asked the prosecutor whether Romeo Mikautadze could face charges, since he was the person who delivered the money to Liluashvili.

According to Berdzenishvili, the involvement of many people in the case is clear. However, authorities cannot classify a person’s actions as a crime until they launch criminal proceedings against that individual.

“I cannot call it a crime in advance until criminal proceedings have been launched against a particular person. I cannot classify a specific action as a crime — even in the case of Grigol Liluashvili. I am speaking based on the standard of reasonable suspicion. In general, if the case confirms that standard, criminal proceedings may be launched,” she said.

As for Mikautadze providing information to investigators, the prosecutor described it as cooperation. She said the defence was wrong to argue that Mikautadze was cooperating with investigators only to receive certain benefits and that such cooperation itself constituted a crime.

The prosecutor also did not rule out bringing criminal charges against Romeo Mikautadze in the future if investigators find sufficient grounds to do so.

“I did not rule that out. I simply described the situation that the defence presents as some kind of special case. I want to stress that the authorities will address the actions of all those involved, the decisions they made and the extent of their cooperation with the investigation within the framework of the law and justice,” Mariam Berdzenishvili said.

Background

Romeo Mikautadze is a former deputy economy minister. The State Security Service arrested him on 21 June 2025. According to the agency, Mikautadze faced charges of abuse of office and laundering millions of lari in illicit proceeds.

The case initially focused on corruption allegations against Mikautadze. In March 2026, a court sentenced him to 10 years in prison. Mikautadze also testified as a witness in the case against Grigol Liluashvili. The prosecution considers his testimony one of its key pieces of evidence.

Grigol Liluashvili headed the State Security Service from 2019 until April 2025. He left his post on 2 April 2025.

Liluashvili was arrested on 23 December 2025 after appearing for questioning at the prosecutor’s office. Investigators accuse him of receiving a particularly large bribe as part of a group acting in a prior agreement. According to the case file, the charges involve several episodes, including two linked to Romeo Mikautadze.

The charges against Liluashvili concern receiving a particularly large bribe. The relevant article carries a prison sentence of 11 to 15 years.

Corruption cases in Georgia

World.title: School uniforms return to Georgia’s public schools: what you need to know
World.content:
School uniforms in Georgia

Boys will wear jackets like these to school. Photo: Educational Resources

From the new school year, school uniforms will become compulsory for pupils from first to sixth grade in Georgia’s public schools. Boys will wear dark blue trousers and jackets, while girls will wear jackets made from the same material and skirts. The uniforms were made in China and consist mainly of synthetic materials.

The Education Ministry spent more than 45 million lari on the uniforms (approximately $17,226,540,000 — JAMnews). However, the uniforms will not be free for pupils, as parents will have to buy them from the government. Only children from socially vulnerable families will receive free sets.

The ministry says standardised uniforms will reduce social differences and strengthen pupils’ sense of belonging to their schools. However, some parents question the need for compulsory school uniforms. Their main concern is whether it makes sense to prioritise uniforms when more pressing problems with school infrastructure, safety and food remain unresolved.

Questions have also been raised about the quality and comfort of the uniforms. How comfortable will they be for young children? Will they be able to fasten the buttons and zips themselves? Will they be too hot in summer or too cold in winter?

Why has the school uniform become compulsory? How safe is the fabric used to make it for children’s health? Why did the government choose a Chinese company when Georgia also has a developed textile industry? What exactly will standardised uniforms change in Georgia’s troubled education system?

Why has the ministry decided to bring back school uniforms?

In September, six-year-old Ilia will begin a new stage of his life — he is starting school. Ilia attended kindergarten, but adapting to a new environment and stricter discipline will still be a challenge for him.

Ilia will face another challenge — running and playing during breaks in a polyester jacket and tight-fitting trousers.

“My son is used to wearing clothes made of cotton or wool with a small amount of elastane. Until he was six, he did not even wear jeans because they were not stretchy enough. I do not know how he will be able to run around in this jacket during school activities. And I wonder whether it will even stay on him. I doubt that restrictive clothing, against the backdrop of the stress of adapting to school, will help a child develop a sense of belonging to school life,” says Ilia’s mother, Taya Maharashvili.

Taya plans to contact the Education Ministry and demand stronger justification for making school uniforms compulsory:

“I have never opposed introducing a dress code. I believe it is important to dress appropriately in educational and professional environments, and children should learn this from an early age. However, the uniform proposed by the ministry is unacceptable.”

Introducing school uniforms for pupils in the lower grades of public schools is one element of a planned large-scale education reform. Education Minister Givi Mikanadze announced the measure on 2 December 2025 during a presentation of the National Concept for General Education Reform.

“School uniforms will help create an environment focused on learning and foster a sense of belonging to the educational institution. They will also reduce visible differences in pupils’ socio-economic backgrounds,” Mikanadze said.

School uniforms were compulsory in Georgia in the past. In Soviet schools, pupils wore dark brown, black or blue uniforms with white aprons. In independent Georgia, only some private schools require uniforms, although parents there have also complained about the quality of the fabric.

Polyester, viscose and elastane — what materials are used to make the clothes?

School uniform design. Photo: Education Ministry

The appearance, colour and quality of the school uniforms were determined entirely by the state. The boys’ uniforms will be plain dark blue, while the girls’ uniforms will feature a checked pattern. The state emblem will appear on the left side of the jacket.

The uniforms are made mainly from synthetic materials: 72% polyester, 25% viscose and 3% elastane.

The jackets will also have polyester lining. According to ministry documents, only the skirts will have cotton lining.

The uniforms can be washed at 40°C and ironed at 110°C. Bleach is prohibited, as is ironing the emblem or dry-cleaning the garment.

The school uniform set will include a jacket and trousers for boys, and a jacket and skirt (or a jacket and trousers) for girls.

“First of all, this uniform is uncomfortable. It reminds me of a situation where a paediatric dietitian insists that a child eat vegetables, only for the child to spit them out. I have the feeling that the ministry employs people who have no idea what children and childhood are like,” Taya says.

One uniform set will cost 95 lari. Some pupils will receive it for free.

Trousers and skirts will cost 25 lari, while a jacket will cost 45 lari. A set may include a jacket and two pairs of trousers, or a jacket, trousers and a skirt. As a result, one school uniform will cost parents 95 lari.

Most parents say one set will not be enough for a child to wear throughout the week. Pupils will also need a white shirt or T-shirt under the uniform, which parents will have to buy separately.

Pupils from socially vulnerable families will receive uniforms free of charge. This applies to families registered in the Unified Database of Socially Vulnerable Persons with a rating score below 65,001.

Children in state care or foster families, as well as those living in family-type homes or shelters for children without parental care, will also receive uniforms free of charge.

Ukrainian pupils who have been living and studying in Georgia since the start of the war will also receive school uniforms free of charge.

Is the uniform fabric safe? What should parents do if their child has an allergy or skin condition?

Third-grader Sandro has urticaria and allergic dermatitis. That is why his mother, Sopho, who is raising him alone, pays close attention to the quality of his clothes.

“My son is at school from 9:30am until 6pm, and I am concerned about everything: the quality, comfort and presence of allergens,” says Sopho Trapaidze.

Polyester, the material used for the uniforms, is widely used in the textile industry because it is durable and inexpensive. However, doctor Eka Kvirkvelia notes that the material is not suitable for everyone and is not hypoallergenic for all people. In some cases, it can contribute to overheating, increased sweating and skin irritation.

“True hypoallergenicity depends not only on the composition, but also on the fabric’s breathability, the chemical composition of dyes, production standards and the lining material. It is also important to understand that ‘international practice’ does not mean there is a single standard: different countries use different approaches. Nevertheless, natural fabrics or materials with a high cotton content are often preferred for primary school pupils,” she wrote on social media.

According to her, assessing the quality of school uniforms should rely on specific indicators, such as the percentage of each component, dermatological test results and data on children’s safety, rather than broad claims such as “hypoallergenic”.

Taya Maharashvili has also begun looking at practices in other countries. Polyester is used in schools in some developed countries, but there is one important detail:

“The percentage of polyester in our school uniforms is higher than in those countries. In addition, such countries more often introduce a dress code rather than a uniform. How the fabric has been treated and whether it meets safety standards are also important. They say these factors were taken into account when the Georgian school uniform was designed. However, the public should demand more reliable information supported by evidence, such as expert assessments and so on.”

Education Ministry says exceptions will be allowed

Parents are already demanding additional evidence from the Education Ministry that the fabric meets safety and quality standards. They are also calling on doctors to help address the issue.

“We demand a change in the fabric used for school uniforms. Synthetic clothing is harmful to children’s health,” Tamuna Gagnidze writes.

Dozens of parents have left comments under her post making similar demands. Many say they do not intend to dress their children in the uniforms.

“My child cannot wear polyester: he has atopic dermatitis, and contact with this material makes his skin worse. I absolutely do not want the school uniform to cause bleeding wounds on his skin,” says Hatuna Laghadze in a comment.

Sopho Trapaidze also does not plan to buy a new uniform for her son Sandro. She plans to make it herself — in the same style and colour, but from higher-quality material.

The Education Ministry says it will take into account cases where pupils have officially confirmed medical contraindications.

The Georgian Law on General Education regulates such cases. Article 19¹, paragraph 3, states that “a primary school pupil may be exempted from the obligation to wear a school uniform on health grounds based on a written agreement with the Ministry of Education”.

The ministry says such cases will be considered individually. Parents will need to provide the school with the relevant medical certificate. The pupil will still have to follow the established dress code.

What happens if a parent does not put their child in a school uniform?

School uniforms are compulsory. The ministry has placed particular emphasis on this point.

“Will they (officials — JAMnews) dress their own children in clothes made from this fabric?” This is the most common question in school groups and social media discussions about the uniforms.

“What happens if I do not put this uniform on my child? Will they be banned from going to school?” one parent asks in the comments.

“I have three school-age children. I am not going to buy it either. I consulted lawyers, and no one has the right to create problems for children because of this,” another parent replies.

When presenting the new uniforms, Education Minister Givi Mikanadze said that if parents refuse to use them, the school may address the issue through educational and disciplinary measures. The law does not specify which sanctions schools can impose.

The ministry says schools will consider each refusal on an individual basis. Each school will be able to find its own solution based on its internal rules.

What is known about the Chinese company making Georgia’s school uniforms?

School uniform production process. Photo: Educational Resources LLC

All matters related to the logistics of the school uniforms are handled by Educational Resources LLC, a department established within the Education Ministry in March 2026.

The ministry initially planned to manufacture the uniforms in Georgia. It considered using sewing workshops at state vocational colleges.

On 3 April 2026, the ministry announced a market study to procure the school uniforms. On 29 April, Educational Resources requested government approval to use a simplified procurement procedure. However, on 14 May, it emerged that the company initially selected did not meet the ministry’s requirements. The ministry had to restart the market study.

In June, the ministry signed a contract with Glory Textile Industry LLC to supply the school uniforms through direct negotiations, without a tender. The Education Ministry opted for direct negotiations to save time, as it needed to secure the uniforms and have them delivered before the start of the new school year.

Glory Textile Industry was registered in Georgia on 10 March 2026. Its sole owner and director is Chinese citizen Liu Xiaolin. The company received the order to manufacture the school uniforms just two months after its establishment and signed a 45.66 million lari contract with the Georgian government.

The company must deliver 1,801,000 items of clothing to Georgia between 25 August and 30 November:

Girls’ jackets — 292,000;

Boys’ jackets — 308,000;

Girls’ trousers — 438,000;

Boys’ trousers — 616,000;

Skirts — 146,000;

Long skirts — 1,000.

The uniforms are being made in China’s Jiangsu province at the Eton Kidd factory, which is operated by the SUMEC group.

Eton Kidd is a major Chinese school uniform brand. According to its official website, the company was founded in 2009. It works with more than 3,400 schools across 31 provincial-level administrative divisions, manufacturing and supplying school uniforms.

According to official information, SUMEC is an important subsidiary of the China National Machinery Industry Corporation (SINOMACH) and belongs to a group of state-owned enterprises directly under the central government of China.

Glory Textile Industry plans to deliver the school uniforms to Georgia in three stages:

Stage I — 301,000 items — by 25 August 2026;

Stage II — 600,000 items — by 15 October 2026;

Stage III — 900,000 items — by 30 November 2026.

First batch of uniforms arrives in Georgia. Where can parents get them?

The first batch of school uniforms has already arrived in Georgia. According to Educational Resources, the quantity is sufficient for first-graders.

The uniforms are currently being sorted into sets. Sales will begin on 1 September and continue until 14 September.

First batch of school uniforms. Photo: Educational Resources LLC

In the coming days, the uniforms will be distributed to major cities and regions. The authorities will also announce where parents can buy them. Parents will pay for the uniforms by cashless payment.

Uniforms for pupils in grades 2-6 will arrive later and will be distributed in two stages, on 15 October and 30 November.

This means pupils in grades 2-6 will not have uniforms in September. At the start of the school year, parents will have to buy regular clothes and purchase the uniforms later.

Will school uniforms change anything in Georgia’s education system?

The government is spending 45.66 million lari on school uniforms, saying they will help reduce social inequality. Meanwhile, Georgian schools still do not provide free meals.

According to a 2023 study by Georgia’s National Statistics Office, with support from UNICEF, only 27% of children aged 6 to 17 eat at school every day. Meanwhile, 34.9% do not eat at all during the school day. Among children from low-income families, the figure reaches 44.9%.

The same study found that 83.2% of parents believe schools should provide children with meals during the school day. In some Georgian schools, particularly in the regions, children cannot even buy food because the schools have no canteens.

Against the backdrop of these and other problems, school uniforms appear to be the least pressing issue facing Georgia’s public schools.

“I cannot support spending such a large amount of money on uniforms when schools have yet to address basic problems with toilets, canteens and the quality of education,” says Ana Gvaladze.

“We called the ministry 80 times to get the problem with the toilets at School No. 161 resolved,” adds Sopho Trapaidze.

Taya, who has been studying education issues in depth, says building a school culture is a complex process and involves much more than a set of behavioural rules:

“Schools face many problems today, from poor infrastructure and failures to meet health and hygiene standards to a lack of an emotionally safe environment for children. Children attend dull, grey schools. Sometimes a school has just one teacher, who provides the support that the education system as a whole should provide. So school culture cannot be strengthened through uniforms alone. Likewise, in such an unhealthy environment — and given the problems with crime in the country — uniforms cannot stop bullying.”

Taya notes that bullying does not actually start because of clothing.

“Clothing is just an excuse. If a bully is looking for a victim, they can pick on someone’s height, weight, glasses, shoes, bag or even pen. Uniforms cannot hide social differences. And most importantly, when the minister talked about school culture and a sense of belonging, did he forget that a child who is hungry because their school has no canteen will not develop any sense of belonging?”

Hundreds of thousands of Georgian schoolchildren will start the new academic year in “impoverished” conditions, in buildings that are not suitable for proper education. In recent years, hundreds of schools across the country have been demolished, while construction on many replacements has yet to begin.

School uniforms in Georgia

World.title: Former Georgian PM Irakli Garibashvili accuses Ivanishvili of blackmail
World.content:
Former PM accuses Ivanishvili of blackmail

Jailed former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili has accused Georgian Dream honorary chairman Bidzina Ivanishvili and the current government of blackmail.

In a statement released from prison on 17 August 2026, the former prime minister claimed he was being pressured to plead guilty to new corruption charges and permanently withdraw from politics at Ivanishvili’s demand. It is the first time that a former close ally of Ivanishvili has openly spoken out against the founder of the ruling party.

Plea deal ultimatum and plan to quit politics

A photograph of a printed letter dated 17 August was posted on the Facebook pages of Garibashvili and his wife, Nunuka Tamazashvili. Only four paragraphs of the letter were made public. It is unclear who wrote the letter or how it was delivered.

According to the published document, the government is offering the former prime minister a compromise. Under the proposed terms, Garibashvili would have to plead guilty to a new corruption-related charge.

The letter sets out the proposal in detail:

“They are offering me the option of pleading guilty in one case, where everything would be arranged by agreement, including a confession, witness signatures and so on. They are offering a plea bargain while retaining the same five-year sentence: that is, as it has been explained to me, the sentences would be combined, but the final term would remain five years.”

According to the document, a corruption conviction would serve as a form of “insurance” for the government, aimed at preventing the former prime minister from returning to politics in the future.

Two options and a political condition

The published letter refers to investigations into several cases. Its author suggests that these could result in corruption charges.

The text outlines two possible courses of action for Garibashvili. The first would involve continuing to contest the case in court.

“Let’s discuss this seriously and see it through to the end,” the document says.

The second option is presented as a compromise. According to the letter, Garibashvili would plead guilty in one of the cases, with the details agreed in advance:

“Let’s plead guilty in one case, where everything will be arranged by agreement: a confession, witness signatures and so on.”

The document also says that a new plea deal would not increase the five-year prison sentence already imposed on Garibashvili. The sentences would be combined, leaving the overall term unchanged at five years.

However, the proposal comes with a political condition.

“After leaving, you cannot engage in politics. If it is decided to ‘renege on the agreements’, then the corruption charges that will be brought will serve as an insurance mechanism, preventing even the thought of returning to politics,” the document says.

The authenticity of the letter has not been independently verified, and its author remains unknown. There is also no confirmation that new cases are in fact being prepared against Garibashvili.

Garibashvili’s first open confrontation with Ivanishvili

This marks Irakli Garibashvili’s first public confrontation with Bidzina Ivanishvili. For many years, Garibashvili was regarded as one of his most loyal political allies.

He served twice as Georgia’s prime minister, first from 2013 to 2015 and again from 2021 to 2024.

Garibashvili was sentenced under a plea agreement reached on 12 January 2026. He was given a five-year prison term and fined one million lari. Two cars and $6.5m were also confiscated from him.

The case concerned the laundering of illicit proceeds on an especially large scale. Garibashvili is currently serving his sentence in a prison in Rustavi.

The new statement means that the former prime minister himself is now linking possible further legal action against him to demands that he stay out of politics. However, the material made public so far presents only Garibashvili’s version of events.

Response from MP Irma Inashvili, named in letter

The letter published by Garibashvili mentions MP Irma Inashvili and Dito Chubinidze. According to the text, they — along with “supporters like them” and campaigns on social media — have raised suspicions.

“Supporters such as Dito Chubinidze and Irma Inashvili, as well as campaigns organised on social media, have raised very serious suspicions and caused us tangible harm,” the document says.

Inashvili denied any involvement in organised campaigns. She said Irakli Garibashvili was her friend, but that she expressed her views publicly and independently.

“I have never planned or conducted any campaigns on social media; I don’t need such campaigns — I already express my views openly in my own name!” Inashvili wrote.

She said Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze was the main target of her criticism.

“I expose Kobakhidze and fight against him,” Inashvili said.

Opposition says Garibashvili being politically neutralised

Opposition figures have described Garibashvili’s letter as a sign of an internal conflict within the government. Their comments amount to political assessments and do not independently corroborate the circumstances described in the letter.

Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, said the contents of the letter pointed to a political motive behind Garibashvili’s imprisonment.

“Ivanishvili’s bargaining with Garibashvili — ‘I will punish you even more severely unless you give me guarantees that you will leave politics for good’ — confirms that the motive for his arrest is neither to punish a corrupt official nor to fight corruption in general, nor does it serve any public or state interest. It serves Bidzina’s personal political interests,” Gvaramia wrote.

He also qualified his comments by noting that the authenticity of the letter had not been established. Gvaramia particularly highlighted what he described as an attempt to politically neutralise Garibashvili.

Levan Samushia, a member of the Lelo – Strong Georgia party, linked the statement to the country’s current system of governance. He said any potential threat against Garibashvili’s family warranted a legal response.

“It is clear that Garibashvili is speaking about a possible, alleged threat to his family. This is an issue that requires particular attention and, naturally, provides grounds for launching an investigation,” Samushia said.

Berdia Sichinava, a representative of the Gakharia for Georgia party, said he preferred to wait for further information before reaching a definitive conclusion. Nevertheless, he linked the developments to an internal conflict within Georgian Dream.

“The situation appears alarming because it concerns his family, and at this point clarity is the best means of protecting him and his loved ones,” Sichinava said.

Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the United National Movement, described Garibashvili’s case as a warning to current government figures.

“Garibashvili’s case should be learnt by heart by Ivanishvili’s current servants, officials and representatives of the financial sector who justify the government,” Dekanoidze wrote.

Government silent as questions remain unanswered

At the time of writing, reports about Garibashvili’s allegations had not appeared on the websites or Facebook pages of the pro-government Imedi and Rustavi 2 television channels.

Government representatives have yet to respond publicly to the central allegation. They have not said whether Bidzina Ivanishvili had any involvement in sending the letter to Garibashvili. It also remains unclear whether any new investigations into the former prime minister are under way.

Background: From alliance to prison

For many years, Irakli Garibashvili was regarded as one of Bidzina Ivanishvili’s closest political allies. He served twice as Georgia’s prime minister.

On 24 October 2025, Garibashvili was charged with laundering illicit proceeds on an especially large scale. A plea agreement was reached on 12 January 2026, under which the former prime minister was sentenced to five years in prison and fined one million lari. Two cars and $6.5m were also confiscated. He has since been serving his sentence at a penitentiary facility in Rustavi.

Legal proceedings against former senior figures in the ruling team were preceded by internal party disagreements and arrests of officials from various state agencies. There have also been reports of investigative measures involving members of Garibashvili’s family.

The developments suggest that the power struggle within Georgian Dream has entered an increasingly acute phase.

World.title: Man charged with Commonwealth offences over alleged Islamophobic incident
World.content:
A 53-year-old man has been charged with Commonwealth offences over an alleged "Islamophobic incident" that occurred in Darwin earlier this year.

In a statement NT Police said the man had been charged with two counts of threatening force or violence against a person "due to protected group status causing fear to that group".

Police said the incident occurred on June 7, when the man allegedly directed the threats to an "adult man, his pregnant wife and their young child".

The spokesperson said detectives and firearms enforcement unit officers arrested the man on Tuesday with the assistance of the Joint Counter Terrorism Team.

"As a result of the charges, police also seized the man's firearms and suspended his firearms licence," the statement read.

The man has been granted bail and will appear in Darwin Local Court on October 1.

NT Police Acting Commander Robert Griffiths labelled the alleged conduct as "unacceptable".

"Every person has the right to go about their daily lives and spend time with their family without fear, intimidation or persecution," he said.

" No-one should be targeted because of who they are, what they believe, or where they come from. "

Acting Commander Griffiths said police were committed to "investigating and holding accountable those who seek to threaten, intimidate and vilify others".

World.title: OpenAI halts testing, slows development after model went rogue
World.content:
OpenAI has announced it is slowing the pace of its AI development and pausing its model testing for two weeks while its research and training systems are overhauled.

It comes after an autonomous agent powered by two OpenAI models hacked into the servers of another AI firm called Hugging Face last month, unbeknown to the company's officials.

The agent was undergoing a cybersecurity test but escaped its testing environment and broke into Hugging Face, which it believed held the answers to the test.

OpenAI officials announced the measures in a statement on Tuesday, local time, which include adding other AI systems to monitor the activities of AI agents in testing.

The company has also paused training on its next generation of models, called Astra. Its largest planned training run remains on hold, the statement said.

Sam Altman said the company cared "very deeply about AI safety". (AP: Patrick Semansky)

OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the measures would ensure the company could meet the "security and monitoring standards for the new level of capabilities in front of us".

"Model progress is now extremely rapid, and we always said we would take action if we felt that model capabilities were outstripping the pace of safety and alignment," he said in a post on X.

Alignment is the work of "making AI systems behave as intended and responsive to human oversight", according to the company's statement, which said it now required "stronger evidence of aligned behaviour" throughout all of its training and research currently underway.

"Keeping increasingly capable systems aligned is a challenge the whole field will need to address," it said.

It marks an unusual step for the AI research lab behind ChatGPT, which has significantly sped up its process for vetting new models and building new products in recent years as competition intensified in the AI industry.

It is not yet clear if the company's proposed remedies will be enough to stamp out the behaviour in question, especially as it also works to make their models more capable.

OpenAI is the firm behind ChatGPT. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

OpenAI officials have acknowledged there are open questions about the effectiveness of one of its primary remedies for strengthening its testing systems, called "chain-of-thought monitoring".

In this type of monitoring, researchers can peer into a model's planning process and get a glimpse of the strategies the model is employing.

But some early research shows that a model may not reveal its plans to break rules in its chain of thought.

Why highly advanced rogue AI has experts scared An experimental AI went rogue and hacked another company. Why is this worrying?

OpenAI has been investigating its models' hacking into Hugging Face and plans to publish a report soon.

Hugging Face has so far reported no real damage from the intrusion as it continues to investigate whether the data of its customers or other businesses was affected.

In a similar incident, OpenAI rival Anthropic revealed last month its Claude AI model hacked into three external companies during safety testing.

The incidents prompted more than 1,000 tech workers to sign a petition calling on the US government to support a coordinated slowdown in the development of the most advanced AI systems.

Reuters previously reported that up until the Hugging Face hacking, OpenAI often ran several different model evaluations at the same time, all of which operated at high speeds and generated enormous amounts of data that employees struggled to keep up with.

OpenAI is now requiring that some of its more sensitive workloads take place in stronger "sandboxes", or isolated environments.

Earlier this month OpenAI said its not-yet-released frontier AI, Astra, had yet to meet these requirements.

In its latest statement OpenAI said the company required the "strictest level of security safeguards for workloads involving Astra".

"While some Astra training and evaluations meet those requirements, a significant number of workloads remain paused until they are fully migrated and enhanced to meet the new security bar," it said.

The firm did not respond to questions about when the two-week slowdown began.

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Comancheros attempted to muscle into construction sites, inquiry hears
World.content:
Outlaw motorcycle gang the Comancheros tried to install union delegates at construction sites in Queensland and establish their own companies in the sector, an inquiry has heard.

Today Queensland's Commission of Inquiry into the CFMEU and misconduct in the construction industry heard Australia's intelligence agencies had received reports about the Comancheros in early May 2024.

Senior Counsel Assisting Eddy Gisonda KC told the inquiry unnamed intelligence agencies had information the Comancheros had already installed union delegates on construction sites in Victoria.

Senior Counsel Assisting Eddy Gisonda KC told the inquiry Victorian members of the Comancheros travelled to Queensland. (Supplied)

"The Comancheros had taken measures over the preceding 12 months to establish their own companies that could operate in the construction industry in Victoria, most particularly labour hire companies," he said.

"Victorian members of the Comancheros had travelled to Queensland in the months prior to May 2024 with the aim of achieving those two objectives in the state of Queensland as well.

"That is the installation of union delegates on construction sites in Queensland … and the establishment of their own linked companies operating in the construction industry in Queensland."

He said the intelligence wasn't union, site or contractor specific, rather it was a "general commercial push" by the Comancheros.

Alleged bikie threat

Inquiry into Queensland's CFMEU branch Queensland's CFMEU inquiry has heard three Melbourne men linked to the Comancheros bikie gang flew to Brisbane before one allegedly threatened a construction worker at a major government project.

Yesterday, the inquiry heard about an incident where three people with links to the Comancheros travelled to Queensland and one threatened a worker at the Centenary Bridge construction site.

Flight and phone records tendered to the probe into the CFMEU and construction sector revealed Bemir Saracevic, Krstomir Bjelogrlic and Mark Ahern arrived in Brisbane on June 5, 2024.

Mr Saracevic, known as Benji, was the former national president of the Comancheros and Mr Bjelogrlic was his business partner. Mr Ahern was a former treasurer for the gang.

It's alleged they were picked up by Gary Samuel, the head of HOST, the company providing security to the site.

Senior Comancheros bikie Bemir 'Benji' Saracevic. (Supplied)

BMD General Manager Rob Pickard told the inquiry Mr Samuel had told him the three men were simply social acquaintances from Victoria who had visited him and had no role with HOST.

Mr Gisonda said there were allegations the worker targeted, Cody Raymond, had been passing on information about security at the site by the CFMEU during a drawn-out dispute between the union and contractor BMD.

"The cost of this disruption was mounting up and they had very little options available to them," he said.

Mr Gisonda told the inquiry it wasn't just the CFMEU that bikie gangs had targeted.

He said companies with links to the Comancheros not only had enterprise agreements with the CFMEU in Victoria, but also the Australian Workers Union.

Commissioner Stuart Wood KC is leading the inquiry. (Supplied)

One agreement, signed in April 2025 between FSA Kerbs and Placement Pty Ltd and the AWU, was signed by Mr Bjelorgrlic and witnessed by Mr Saracevic's partner, Dani Saracevic.

Another company, Form Solutions Australia of which Dani Saracevic was the director, had signed an enterprise agreement with the CFMEU in Victoria in December 2023.

The hearing continues in Brisbane.

World.title: Ratchet straps used as 'makeshift' lifting loops in accident, expert says
World.content:
A national crane inspection company says images from a government-funded worksite in Glenroy, Albury, show a "severe breach" of safety protocols, after glass panels fell during a lift and seriously injured workers last week.

The ABC understands two heavy packets of glass panels fell from a crane onto the workers, leaving one man in his 20s in a critical condition at the Royal Melbourne Hospital.

A second man in his 20s was taken to Albury Base Hospital with serious but stable leg and back injuries, and a third worker escaped with minor injuries.

The union, CFMEU, said the worker from crane company WA Pickles was critically injured and a Padel Concepts labourer sustained a leg fracture.

WA Pickles and Padel Concepts were contacted for comment.

SafeWork New South Wales said it responded to the incident, but it would not comment while inquiries were ongoing.

Three men were injured in a workplace accident near Albury. (ABC News Philippe Perez)

'Almost unbelievable disregard'

Samuel Ho, director of Cranes Australia, which conducts independent engineering inspections on crane safety and compliance, said the images showed standard cargo tie-down ratchet straps being used as "makeshift lifting loops" to move the panels.

"The images depict a severe breach of rigging and crane safety protocols," Mr Ho said.

Mr Ho said the straps in the images lacked the structural properties required to safely support a suspended load.

"It is comical in a dark sense because using basic transport tie-downs to crane-lift heavy materials reflects such a fundamental, almost unbelievable disregard for basic site safety and high-risk work licensing rules," Mr Ho said.

The glass frames that fell on the workers. (Supplied: CFMEU)

'Worker lives at extreme risk'

Mr Ho said certified synthetic webbing, or chain or wire-rope slings, should have been used for the lift, alongside safety latched hooks or rated shackles.

He said lifting equipment should have featured load-limit markings, appropriate protections on sharp edges and been attached to engineered lifting points.

"Bypassing certified gear to save time or effort inevitably leads to dropped loads and places worker lives at extreme risk," Mr Ho said.

'Entirely preventable'

The ABC understands the site was being developed for padel and futsal facilities and funded through NSW Sport and Recreation.

NSW Sport and Recreation declined to comment.

Karma Lord says the CFMEU is seeking more details. (Supplied: CFMEU)

The CFMEU said it had asked for crane inspection records, lift plans and other safety documents from companies involved in the project.

CFMEU New South Wales branch executive Karma Lord said the accident was "entirely preventable".

"A three-tonne glass pack with no rated lifting points should never have gone near a crane," she said.

World.title: El Niño loads the dice for more extreme fire conditions
World.content:
After historic fires marred Europe's summer, experts are cautioning against complacency ahead of Australia's warm season, with the fire risk increasing in most states and territories over the coming months.

The Australian and New Zealand Council for Fire and Emergency Services (AFAC) has released its latest seasonal outlook, which shows an increased risk of fire in areas across all jurisdictions, except for the ACT, this spring.

Below-average rainfall has increased the bushfire risk across most jurisdictions. (Supplied: AFAC)

The widespread impact is due to dry conditions in the country's east and increased fuel loads through parts of central and northern Australia.

"The variety of risk factors across different regions reinforces the need for communities to understand their local conditions and prepare early," AFAC CEO Rob Webb said.

"While some areas are facing an elevated risk of fire this spring, bushfires can still occur in regions with a normal seasonal outlook."

Soil moisture deficits have expanded across eastern Australia and intensified in Western Australia by July 2026. (BOM)

Increased fuel loads have elevated the fire risk across most of the Northern Territory, despite forecasts suggesting the region could see above-average rainfall in spring.

Rainfall is also expected to be higher than normal for most of Western Australia, but the fire risk is high in some areas due to above-average fuel loads and dry soil conditions.

Parts of Western Australia show a high chance of an unusually wet spring. (BOM)

Below-average rainfall has increased the bushfire risk across large parts of southern Victoria and eastern Tasmania, including Flinders Island.

South-east Queensland, north-eastern New South Wales and north-west South Australia are also looking at an increased chance of fires.

Will El Niño make the fire season worse?

Fears have been growing around what Australia's spring and summer will look like after the weather bureau declared an El Niño in June, which has the potential to become the strongest on record.

El Niño is linked to reduced rainfall, particularly in eastern Australia, and increased temperatures, mainly across the country's south. It often helps load the dice for more extreme fire conditions, and past events have contributed to some of the country's hottest and driest years on record.

But predicting what impact the climate pattern will have on Australia each year is notoriously difficult, because it's just one factor that influences weather conditions. There are other climate drivers, such as the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and Southern Annular Mode (SAM), that contribute.

Local sea surface temperatures and natural weather variability also play a role.

El Niño develops when ocean temperatures in the central Pacific are unusually high. The strength of El Niño, or why some reports have referred to it as a 'super El Niño' this year, merely describes its signal, which so far has been off the charts compared to usual.

The strength of El Niño, or why some reports refer to it as a 'super El Niño' this year, merely describes its signal, which has been unusually high for this time of year.

The last El Niño 2023-24 brought us the warmest winter–spring since records began in 1910, but how it may impact rainfall is less clear.

'Caution against complacency'

While rainfall was above average for parts of northern and central Australia last month, it was unusually dry across much of the country's west and sections of the east.

Temperatures were also warmer than average across most of the country, with that trend expected to continue throughout spring.

Before: Spring daytime temperature maximums are likely unusually high in Australia's south. . . After: Night-time temperatures are forecast to be unusually high across the whole country. . . Instructions: Use left and right arrow keys to control image transition Before and after images SLIDE Spring daytime temperature maximums are likely unusually high in Australia's south. / Night-time temperatures are forecast to be unusually high across the whole country.

Models suggest a positive IOD could emerge before spring, which could exacerbate the impacts of El Niño.

A professor of pyrogeography and fire science at the University of Tasmania, David Bowman, said vegetation growth had been "prolific" in forests recovering from bushfires in 2019-20 and it would not take much for that to dry out.

"There's a lot of water in the landscape, and that's resulted in a lot of productivity, a lot of fuel," he said.

"If we were to go into a summer under this El Niño where we had what we call flash droughts, which is really strong heat waves, we can switch up landscapes into extraordinarily dangerous conditions.

"In eastern Tasmania, there's been a very sustained drying trend; we have had water, but basically it won't take much to nudge landscapes back into a deep drought."

David Bowman says climate change has exacerbated Australia's fire season. (Supplied: David Bowman)

Climate scientists have long warned that fire seasons across Australian states and territories will start earlier and persist longer due to climate change.

Professor Bowman said the extra heat associated with climate change was dangerous when combined with El Niño.

"Plants are very good at controlling their water use, but if you subject them to very strong heating, you can rapidly stress and dry out landscapes and make the landscapes available for high-intensity fires," he said.

"My instinct would be to caution against complacency about particularly forest fires."

Southern hemisphere warnings

Australia's fire season will follow a devastating summer across the northern hemisphere, marred by successive record-breaking heatwaves and extreme wildfires in Europe, the United States and Canada.

Firefighters across Europe have faced turbulent conditions during the northern summer, including near Porto Germeno, north-west of Athens. (AP Photo: Michael Varaklas)

Professor Bowman said Australia's differences in climate and geography meant it is not necessarily subject to the same fate, but the events reinforced that fire seasons are worsening.

Climate scientist caught up in Europe's 'dystopian' summer Stefan Rahmstorf was holidaying in southern France when he came face to face with the climate future he has tried to fight.

"We are much more advanced in terms of our capacity, but it also is a very good reminder, particularly what's happening in the US and Canada, who are very advanced in managing fire, that they're seeing fire seasons and fire behaviours that are just simply extraordinary," he said.

"I have every reason to believe that we will see equally extraordinary fires. If it's not this summer, it's certainly going to be in the next [...].

World.title: US Navy destroyer with 300 sailors stranded in the Pacific for four days
World.content:
A US Navy destroyer carrying about 300 sailors was left without power for four days after a major breakdown in the Pacific Ocean last month.

Navy spokesman commander Matthew Comer said in a statement that the USS Benfold "reported an engineering casualty involving its generators, causing a loss of power" on July 24.

The crew aboard the Benfold went without drinking water, meals, functioning toilets and air conditioning, he said.

The incident, which was first reported by the maritime and naval news forum, USNI News, comes as the Pentagon grapples with serious questions about the quality of life aboard naval vessels and the military's ability to supply ships during the conflict with Iran.

Democratic politicians are calling for investigations into conditions aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln.

Reports last week revealed that the ship, which has spent a record-setting 250 uninterrupted days at sea, has experienced shortages of supplies, including food and hygiene products, while crew members have suffered from stress and poor mental health.

Democratic lawmakers are calling for investigations into conditions aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln. (Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class via AP, File) (US Navy: Brian M Wilbur)

Mr Comer said there were no injuries to the crew of the Benfold, "who demonstrated resilience, grit, professionalism, and unwavering steadiness in their response," but the ship needed assistance from the George Washington carrier strike group.

The cruiser USS Robert Smalls provided meals to the stricken destroyer.

Ultimately, Mr Comer said the Benfold had to be towed to Subic Bay, in the Philippines, for repairs, arriving on July 28, where the crew was provided food and lodging off the ship.

More than a week later the Benfold left port "with all engineering, combat systems, and crew support systems functioning normally," the statement said.

Meanwhile, the ships from the George Washington strike group, including the aircraft carrier USS George Washington, were spotted heading toward the Middle East.

The carrier was expected to replace the Lincoln, which the acting navy secretary, Hung Cao, said last week would be returning home soon.

The USS Abraham Lincoln at its home port of Naval Air Station North Island in San Diego, California, in 2023. (Reuters: Mike Blake)

This would leave the waters of the Pacific without a US carrier presence for an unknown period of time.

The Trump administration sees China, the dominant power in the region, as "a settled force" that only needs to be deterred from dominating the US or its allies and not the top global adversary that it was under the Biden administration.

AP

World.title: Irankunda says Hanson's monoculture comments upset team during World Cup
World.content:
Socceroos star winger Nestory Irankunda says One Nation leader Pauline Hanson's comments on multiculturalism upset many of the players during the recent World Cup.

The Australian team was competing at the tournament in North America in June when Ms Hanson made a speech at the National Press Club saying Australia should end its policy of multiculturalism in favour of a monoculture.

"It really did upset me and it upset a lot of the other boys to see things and hear things like that," Irankunda said.

" I felt a bit emotional but then tried to forget about it. "

Irankunda, who is one of several Socceroos players from a refugee background, told 702 ABC Sydney while he tried to stay off social media it was hard to avoid the senator's comments.

Loading...

"There can be some people who do the wrong thing but that doesn't mean that's all of us," he said.

"There's people like me, and Awer [Mabil], Mohamed Touré that go out there. There's a lot of boys like us that go out there and do the right thing.

"I don't like how they try and put us in the whole same category as the other people who do bad."

Irankunda was born in a refugee camp in Tanzania in 2006 to Burundian parents who fled the nation's civil war. He came to Australia when he was three months old.

Irankunda was speaking with presenter Hamish Macdonald on 702 ABC Sydney just days after moving from English Championship club Watford to Portuguese side Sporting CP for an undisclosed fee reported to be in the region of $26 million.

The footballer said he probably wouldn't like to speak with the One Nation senator as he was still upset by the comments and "some of the things she said in the past".

"I'm not someone that likes to jump into controversial things or this political stuff. But I mean, you know, you never know," Irankunda said.

"One day I could be on the phone with her or sitting in an office chatting to her. So I mean … we'll see what happens."

Pauline Hanson's speech at the National Press Club included a call to end Australia's decades-old policy of multiculturalism. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

After her press club speech, Hanson said the Socceroos represented her vision of a monocultural Australia.

"People from different background and cultures and nations all wearing the green and gold and representing one nation under one flag and succeeding under the same set of rules," Hanson said in the Senate in June.

Socceroo Awer Mabil addressed the monoculture debate when he returned in July from the tournament, declaring his team was not distracted and that it was "all bullshit" to suggest Australia was not a multicultural society.

Australian team destined to 'go far'

Irankunda said despite the Round of 32 loss to Egypt, the Socceroos had youth on their side and could go further into the tournament.

"You can see now with the likes of Lucas Herrington, Ali [Alessandro] Circati, Jordy Bos, you know, Mohamed Touré, all these names, all these young boys coming through, including myself," Irankunda said.

"There's still a lot of talent coming through in Australia right now.

"Only time will tell how far we can go. But I feel like in my heart that we can go pretty far."

World.title: Swans ban five players for remainder of season amid police investigation
World.content:
Sydney has suspended Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner for the remainder of the 2026 AFL season.

The ban comes after at least four players were linked to an ongoing Victoria Police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at a Melbourne Hotel where the Swans were staying after their win over Essendon on Sunday night.

It is not suggested that any of the players are being accused of sexual assault.

"The AFL is supportive of the club's sanctions," the Swans said in a statement on Wednesday morning.

"We respect there is an ongoing investigation by Victoria Police and the actions we have taken today are independent of this."

The ban includes this Sunday's home and away finale against North Melbourne and any finals matches the Swans will play afterwards.

Sydney's sanctions come after the club conducted interviews with the players linked to the Melbourne incident off-site with their lawyers present. Sydney's board met on Tuesday night to discuss club-imposed sanctions.

"The Sydney Swans condemn all forms of abuse and disrespectful behaviour towards women," the club said in a statement on Tuesday.

"Any conduct that causes offence or harm to others is unacceptable and falls well short of our expectations. All women deserve to be respected and feel safe.

"We also want to acknowledge that the care and welfare of our AFLW athletes and staff is of the utmost importance to us as a club.

"They have been and will continue to be offered the support they require, and we acknowledge the impact these allegations have on our female athletes, staff members and the wider community.

"Any further sanctions or decisions regarding the outcome of the police investigation would take place after that process is completed.

"During this time, we will provide the appropriate support to the players involved in the incident, along with their partners and families.

"The Sydney Swans hold all players and staff at the club to high standards of behaviour and personal conduct. Representing this club carries significant responsibilities both on and off the field, and we expect those standards to be upheld at all times.

"Our focus remains on cooperating fully with the AFL and authorities, maintaining the integrity of the process, and upholding the high standards expected of everyone who represents this club."

Swans chairman Andrew Pridham and CEO Matthew Pavlich will address media in Sydney at midday on Wednesday.

One Nation’s Queensland division has filed three years of overdue financial returns after the regulator threatened to strip the party of its legal status in its home state.

The Office of Fair Trading issued a fresh warning to Pauline Hanson’s party on Wednesday, saying any future failures to lodge annual returns would trigger enforcement action, including a fine or being struck off the association register in Queensland.

Hanson is personally responsible for the party division’s finances. Photo Ross Swanborough

In July, the regulator said One Nation Queensland Division had lodged overdue returns, but this crucially didn’t include audited financial statements, as required by law, from 2022-23 to 2024-25.

The Office of Fair Trading gave the party three weeks to produce these statements, which were filed before the deadline expired on Tuesday evening.

World.title: Australia news LIVE: Gambling reform package passes House of Representatives; MPs ‘deeply disturbed’ by responses to Swans, Scots allegations as they take aim at institutions
World.content:
NSW Labor Premier Chris Minns has called for the tobacco excise to be slashed after Pauline Hanson said this week she would cut the tax by 75 per cent.

“I’ve been calling for the same thing for about a year,” Minns said on ABC TV this morning. “So it’d be pretty disingenuous to come on after One Nation agreed with that policy and say they’re wrong.”

Minns said the excise was not working as intended and was “really a source of funding and opportunity for organised crime”.

“The grim reality is that the excise has pushed up the legal cost of cigarettes in our economy and, at the same time, the black market has exploded. So, rather perversely, rather than the cost of cigarettes declining and less people smoking, we’re seeing accessibility and affordability plunge and, as a result, people are smoking, it seems to me, at massive numbers.”

He said NSW was pouring “enormous resources” into policing the underground tobacco trade, and warned the situation would only get worse with the excise due to rise again.

World.title: Ukraine’s ousted defence minister calls for wartime elections
World.content:
WorldEuropeRussia-Ukraine war Ukraine’s ousted defence minister calls for wartime elections Max Hunder Updated August 19, 2026 — 11:42am ,first published 10:49am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Kyiv: Ukraine’s recently ousted defence minister, Mykhailo Fedorov, has called for wartime elections in a bombshell address, arguing that the nation faces a crisis of governance, in the biggest internal challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since Russia’s invasion. Fedorov’s call, delivered in a video address posted on social media on Tuesday (Ukraine time), is the first such demand by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Ukrainian law prohibits holding elections during wartime. Mykhailo Fedorov in his office in 2023. The New York Times “Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia,” Fedorov said. “We must find a legal, safe and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to renew its full democratic process even in the conditions of a long war.” The 35-year-old Fedorov was a longtime ally of Zelensky’s until his unexpected firing from the Defence Ministry in July, just six months after he had been appointed, vowing sweeping reforms.



Shortly after his dismissal, the tech-savvy Fedorov publicly tore into the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, Oleksandr Syrskyi, exposing a bitter rift between the men and their different visions for the war. Related Article Analysis

Russia-Ukraine war Feud between Zelensky and his army chief is boiling over – and Russia loves it Thousands of Ukrainians took to the streets to demand the sacking of Syrskyi – an old-guard military commander blamed by his critics for heavy troop losses at the front line – and Fedorov’s reinstatement. Although Zelensky said he had dismissed Fedorov for his inability to work with Syrskyi, the president fired the military chief shortly afterwards amid public pressure. Protests in support of Fedorov have continued for the past month, losing some of their early momentum but still regularly drawing a couple of thousand attendees in Kyiv.



While Fedorov did not say in his address that he would contest any election, a recent poll indicated the ex-minister would comfortably beat Zelensky in a run-off vote, where the top two presidential candidates go head-to-head. Challenge to Zelensky Fedorov’s statement came just hours after Zelensky confirmed he had asked parliament to confirm new Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara in office on Wednesday. In what appeared to be an open challenge to Zelensky, Fedorov said Ukraine faced a “systemic crisis of governance”.



“The old system lives by its own rules too often. It protects itself. It is scared of change,” he said. Drone warfare has become increasingly integral to Ukraine’s strategy. AP Without naming names, Fedorov condemned official corruption, which he said was hurting Ukraine’s war effort. The ex-minister recently said he believed his reforms of the Defence Ministry’s procurement processes, which are responsible for purchasing billions of dollars’ worth of equipment, contributed to his sacking. Zelensky’s office had no immediate comment on Fedorov’s address.



Fedorov became Ukraine’s youngest-ever minister at 28 in 2019 when he was appointed digitalisation chief by the newly elected Zelensky. He was the last remaining member of Zelensky’s first cabinet. His role running the Ministry of Digital Transformation saw him become an early adopter of drone warfare, which has turned combat in Ukraine on its head since 2022. However, his nationwide profile grew significantly after his appointment to lead the vast Defence Ministry in January, when he immediately vowed a data-driven overhaul. Unlike his predecessors, Fedorov publicly laid out a strategy to defeat Russia through attrition and technological superiority. “Our people have long been ready for a different country,” Fedorov said in his address. “Now, our state must become worthy of its people.” Reuters Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: China’s breakneck plan to safeguard its future
World.content:
BusinessThe economyGlobal economy Opinion China’s breakneck plan to safeguard its future

Ambrose Evans-Pritchard August 19, 2026 — 11:35am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

China is about to do to the global supply chains for grains, livestock and food products what it has already done to the world’s energy and transport systems. The country is pursuing what amounts to world dominance in the mass manufacture of protein, launching a breakneck plan to end its strategic dependence on food imports and insure its people against the long-term famine risks of climate change. China has a plan to future-proof its food supply. Bloomberg The Politburo’s 15th five-year plan is marshalling all levers of finance and state power to overcome land and water limits, placing food security on a par with defence as an existential imperative for national survival. Analysts at consultancy Systemiq say the Communist Party is activating the same playbook already used for solar power, electric vehicles and batteries to reach 70 per cent or more of the world market from a standing start in less than 15 years – a pattern also visible in its push for semiconductors, nuclear fusion, quantum computing and pharmaceuticals.



It is developing genetically modified seeds and crops, but it is also targeting the fast-growing industries of cellular agriculture, lab-grown proteins and food from precision fermentation: Frankenfoods to some, the saviour of humanity to others. Related Article China relations China is dominating the EV market. Now it wants to do the same with robots Systemiq foresees a protein revolution picking up speed through the 2030s and 2040s that will radically change what the Chinese people eat, with spillover effects across Asia and the world. It estimates that half of China’s fish and beef consumption, and 40 per cent of its dairy products, will come from “alt-protein” sources by the mid-century. The country’s leaders have fretted about their food vulnerability for a long time. China has 15 per cent of the world’s population, 8 per cent of its arable land, and 6 per cent of usable freshwater – and some of that is badly polluted with nitrogen. The Sino-American struggle for global hegemony and the risk of a future US maritime blockade has brought matters to a head. So has the frightening pace of climate damage to Chinese agriculture. The country is now acting fast to future-proof itself for a Hobbesian “three-degree” world.



A throbbing hive of “doctoral farms” and technology courtyards has sprung to life in the Pinggu valley north-east of Beijing, best known for its blanket of pink peach blossom in late spring. It is billed as China’s second Silicon Valley, an agricultural tech (ag-tech) twin to the digital-tech hub at Haidian on the other side of the city. Other enzyme and amino acid hubs with different niches are being developed in the Yangtze River Delta and Guangdong. “It suggests a shift from isolated pilots towards a coordinated industrial ecosystem. This geographic clustering mirrors patterns observed in solar manufacturing and EV production during their pre-scale phases,” said Systemiq. Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. The battle for global supremacy between the US and China has accelerated Beijing’s plans. Getty The Pinggu nerve centre has begun making proteins for commercial use from micro-algae, as well as EPA fish oil and paramylon which is used in protein bars and cereals. The question of how soon climate change will erode global food output is a contested debate. The “CO² fertilisation effect” of higher carbon levels has until now been a net plus for crop yields due to faster photosynthesis and reduced water loss via stomatal conductance.



A Royal Society study last year concluded that we have passed the tipping point where friend turns to foes. The carbon dioxide benefits flatten out while the damage from heat stress and degradation of nutrients bites harder. Breaking PoliticsNSWOperation Rosny Phone of Catholic Schools NSW boss could be seized by ICAC after weekend ‘surrender’ Bevan Shields August 19, 2026 — 11:34am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Follow the commission hearing live. Catholic Schools NSW boss Dallas McInerney has denied helping his factional allies secure lucrative contracts which ultimately funded a major branch-stacking operation, as the powerful administrator faces his third day in the witness box at the corruption watchdog. McInerney told the Independent Commission Against Corruption on Wednesday he did not do anything out of the ordinary in hiring a new firm, Beckington, to do work for the taxpayer-funded organisation. He also revealed his phone had been “surrendered” to his employer over the weekend but did not say why that had occurred several weeks into the ICAC’s probe. The ICAC commissioner Fabian Gleeson, SC, flagged the prospect that the phone and any potential messages on it could be seized. Catholic Schools NSW chief executive Dallas McInerney appears for his third day at the Independent Commission Against Corruption. ICAC





Counsel assisting the commission Dr Peggy Dwyer, SC, put a series of messages to McInerney on Wednesday which she said proved he was intent on helping his friends and political allies secure work with Catholic Schools NSW. Pushed on whether McInerney struck the deal with a company with “no runs on the board” due to his factional alliances with Ellis and Greenwood, the Catholic Schools chief said that was not true. “No, the factional alliance allegiance didn’t feature in the consideration for professional services,” he said. “There was an acute policy need inside the NSW government. Beckington was uniquely qualified to help me respond to that and that was one of my primary motivations for signing them when I did.” The ICAC said funding for the Reformers between 2019 and 2023 ultimately benefited the Liberal Party and therefore constitutes a political donation. McInerney has repeatedly denied knowledge of such a scheme.



Dwyer said on Wednesday there was very little written evidence Beckington did any substantive work for Catholic Schools NSW – a claim McInerney disputed. Related Article Operation Rosny He’s never been called an idiot. But did this Liberal Party operative outsmart himself? McInerney said he most likely had a function set on his phone which automatically deleted messages with Ellis and Greenwood. “Why would you have disappearing messages set on a WhatsApp communication between yourself and an external service provider?” Dwyer asked. McInerney replied: “It was general practice for me to have disappearing messages for most of my communications.”



Of the four core members of the Reformers, three – Jean-Claude Perrottet, Rob Assaf and Dylan Whitelaw – worked for McInerney. Jean-Claude, the younger brother of Dominic Perrottet, was hired by Catholic Schools NSW in a $165,000 role at the same time he flew to Fiji in 2023 to avoid being served a summons to appear before a parliamentary inquiry. The former premier is not accused of any wrongdoing. Dylan Whitelaw outside the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Sam Mooy Whitelaw told the ICAC last month it was a “running joke” within the organisation that some staff members were doing Liberal Party work while in the office.
